summary: The project aims to detect and monitor areas in Bolivia vulnerable to soil erosion using satellite technologies, artificial intelligence, and drone simulation. Data from NASA covering vegetation, precipitation, and soil moisture is used to identify high-risk areas and generate specific coordinates of interest. Subsequently, machine learning models are applied to recognize signs of erosion within imagery. details: What It Does & How It WorksOur project is an integrated geospatial intelligence and early warning platform designed to detect, monitor, and prevent soil erosion disasters in vulnerable regions such as Cochabamba, Bolivia. It combines satellite data analysis, Machine Learning, tactical routing, and automated community alerts into a single workflow:Satellite & Environmental Data Ingestion: The system gathers Earth observation datasets and terrain variables (such as slope, soil moisture, and vegetation/ground cover) using NASA Earthdata access protocols. Machine Learning Erosion Detection: A trained ML model analyzes satellite imagery and environmental parameters to classify soil instability and predict erosion risk levels (low, medium, and high), exporting the results as geospatial layers (JSON/GeoJSON).Interactive Dashboard & Tactical Waypoint Routing: A unified web platform merges a live environmental monitoring panel with an interactive tactical map. The dashboard overlays the ML erosion risk zones directly onto planned field routes and waypoints, automatically flagging paths that intersect critical erosion areas so teams can recalculate safer trajectories.Automated WhatsApp Early Warning System: Whenever sensor telemetry or ML predictions exceed safe thresholds, a backend trigger automatically dispatches geolocation-tagged alerts via the WhatsApp API to local community leaders (comunarios) and municipal emergency authorities (such as Risk Management Units / UGR).BenefitsProactive Disaster Prevention: Shifts risk management from reactive emergency response to early detection before catastrophic landslides or soil collapse occur.Zero-Barrier Communication: Delivers critical warnings directly through WhatsApp—a platform already used daily by rural and peri-urban populations—eliminating the need for residents to download specialized apps or interpret complex GIS maps.Safer Field Logistics: Protects field teams, farmers, and transport routes by cross-referencing navigation waypoints against real-time soil stability predictions.Unified Situational Awareness: Consolidates satellite analytics, ground monitoring, and alert logs into one accessible interface for decision-makers.Intended ImpactThe project aims to safeguard human lives, agricultural livelihoods, livestock, and critical road infrastructure in erosion- and landslide-prone valleys and slopes across Cochabamba (such as Tiquipaya, Sacaba, and Colomi). By translating complex satellite data and Machine Learning outputs into clear, actionable alerts, the platform bridges the gap between scientific Earth observation and grassroots community resilience. Furthermore, its modular architecture allows it to be replicated and scaled to other vulnerable Andean and rural regions worldwide.Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & SoftwareProgramming Languages: Python (data pipelines, ML modeling, threshold evaluation, and API triggers), HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript (interactive dashboard and monitoring interface).Data Science & Machine Learning: Jupyter Notebooks, Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn / TensorFlow, and NASA Earthdata / OPeNDAP data access configurations (.dodsrc). Geospatial & Web Visualization: Interactive web mapping libraries (Leaflet) with custom GeoJSON/JSON risk overlays and responsive telemetry cards.Alerting & Backend Integration: WhatsApp Cloud API / Twilio API for automated message dispatching, python-dotenv for secure credential management, and structured JSON/database storage for contact segmentation and alert logging.Development Environment: Visual Studio Code, Git/GitHub for collaborative version control, and isolated Python virtual environments (env). How Our Project Is CreativeDynamic Intersection of ML and Routing: Rather than displaying Machine Learning predictions as a static map, our system actively cross-references predicted erosion polygons with tactical waypoints to alert users when a planned route crosses unstable ground.Audience-Aware Dual Messaging: The alert engine translates the exact same environmental anomaly into two tailored formats: simple, actionable safety guidance with a direct Google Maps pin for local community members, and technical severity metrics (erosion index, moisture levels, and exact coordinates) for emergency authorities.Factors Considered by Our TeamRural Connectivity & Digital Literacy: Recognizing that remote communities often face limited bandwidth and may not use specialized software, we prioritized lightweight web rendering and WhatsApp messaging for maximum reach.Preventing Alert Fatigue: We implemented cooldown timers and severity thresholds so communities and authorities are not flooded with repetitive notifications during prolonged weather events.System Performance & Reliability: By decoupling heavy ML inference from front-end map rendering via standardized JSON/GeoJSON outputs, the dashboard remains fast and reliable even on modest hardware.Modular Teamwork & Scalability: We organized the project into clean, decoupled directories (data, notebooks, src, results, web) so team members working on satellite extraction, Machine Learning, front-end dashboards, and alert APIs could integrate their work seamlessly
